incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p95 runtime latency spike detected after deploy release/2026-03-15-canary. p95 > 1.2s for last 5m across canary pool. Paging oncall @Maria
Maria (oncall): Oncall ack. Looking at console now — link: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/runtime/canary-latency
Jake: I rolled the canary ~15m ago, change was: reduced batching window from 8ms->2ms + kernel affinity tweak to prefer new kernel path.
Priya: Seeing kernel fallback on 8/24 canary nodes: logs show "kernel_select: fallback_to_generic" and increased syscall wait.
Leo: Node metrics show increased context switches and queue depth rising on affected hosts. Might be kernel/kmod path mismatch after the affinity change.
Maria (oncall): Confirming customer errors? Any 5xx spike?
Amanda (CS): Yes, we have 3 customers reporting slow responses on chat endpoints (Enterprise-Alpha, RetailX, AdPlatform). No widespread 5xx yet, but timeouts for long completions. CS notified P1 for Enterprise-Alpha.
Jake: Ok, immediate mitigation options: 1) flip safety toggle to restore previous batching behavior 2) reduce canary traffic to 0% 3) emergency rollback of canary release.
Priya: If kernel fallback is the cause, restoring batching might avoid the hot path that triggers fallback. But fallback seems deterministic on some host configs.
Maria (oncall): Can we flip the safety toggle remotely? Which flag?
Jake: Flag name is runtime.batch_window_override and runtime.kernel_affinity_enable. The "safety toggle" endpoint is internal feature toggle service. Command: ```curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/toggle -d '{"flag":"runtime.batch_window_override","value":"8ms","env":"canary"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'```
Maria (oncall): Trying safety toggle now.
ops-bot: action_log: Maria triggered feature toggle runtime.batch_window_override -> 8ms (canary) by Maria at 3333330120
Priya: Monitoring... latency p95 improved on 2 nodes but still high on others. Kernel fallback events persist.
Leo: Suggest reducing canary traffic to isolate. We can shift kubernetes Istio route to 10% then 0%.
Maria (oncall): Routing change in progress: ```kubectl patch trafficsplit canary -p '{"spec":{"canaryWeight":10}}'```
deploy-bot: deploy-log: trafficshift canary -> 10% by Maria at 3333330260
Amanda (CS): Heads up - Enterprise-Alpha is on the canary pool. CS will pause any heavy test runs and notify them of degraded perf.
Jake: After traffic shift to 10% we still see some slow tails from the remaining canary hosts. I recommend emergency rollback of the canary commit; prepare revert to release/2026-03-14-stable.
Priya: Agree. Rolling back should remove the kernel-affinity change and batching tweak. Eviction risk minimal if we scale down properly.
Maria (oncall): Initiating rollback. deploy-bot, kick revert.
deploy-bot: release-revert: started revert of release/2026-03-15-canary -> release/2026-03-14-stable by Maria at 3333331500
ops-bot: action_log: draining canary hosts before revert, disabling new connections.
Leo: Drains show active sessions -> we'll allow graceful 30s.
Priya: Kernel fallback events drop immediately on drained hosts. Metrics trending back to baseline.
Maria (oncall): Revert completed. deploy-bot reports traffic on stable path restored to 100% at 3333331800.
deploy-bot: release-revert: completed successfully at 3333331800 (no rollback errors)
incident-bot: Recovery: p95 latency back within SLOs across canary/stable pools. Post-revert monitoring window begins (30m).
Amanda (CS): Customer impact summary so far: 3 customers affected by high latency, Enterprise-Alpha saw several timed-out requests. CS will follow up with incident template and targeted outreach.
Jake: Root cause hypothesis: kernel affinity tweak + smaller batching window caused atypical kernel code path to be exercised on certain host kernels, causing fallback to generic kernels and increased syscall latency. Repro steps needed in staging with same kernel versions.
Priya: Action items: 1) Run canary DAG on staging kernels matching affected hosts 2) Add automated detection for kernel_fallback events to earlier signal 3) Revert change from codebase and re-evaluate batching defaults.
Maria (oncall): I'll hand this to next oncall for monitoring and postmortem coordination. Oncall handoff: @Priya will lead postmortem, @Jake to provide the rollout diff and repro, @Leo to gather host kernel versions, @Amanda to lead customer comms.
Priya: I'll own the postmortem, setting preliminary bridge and doc. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD.
Maria (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving the thread to postmortem. If latency resurfaces tag @Maria and escalate. :white_check_mark:
Amanda (CS): Noted. CS will send initial outreach in 45m.
incident-bot: note: paging closed at 3333335400 after stability window met.
Maria (oncall): closing incident oncall. Follow-up items posted to #postmortems and assigned in JIRA.
